content.content:
1→---
     2→title: logging
     3→description: Configure logging behavior in the terminal when running Next.js in development mode, including fetch logging, incoming requests, and forwarding browser console logs to the terminal.
     4→---
     5→
     6→{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}
     7→
     8→## Options
     9→
    10→<AppOnly>
    11→
    12→### Fetching
    13→
    14→You can configure the logging level and whether the full URL is logged to the console when running Next.js in development mode.
    15→
    16→```js filename="next.config.js"
    17→module.exports = {
    18→  logging: {
    19→    fetches: {
    20→      fullUrl: true,
    21→    },
    22→  },
    23→}
    24→```
    25→
    26→Any `fetch` requests that are restored from the [Server Components HMR cache](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/serverComponentsHmrCache) are not logged by default. However, this can be enabled by setting `logging.fetches.hmrRefreshes` to `true`.
    27→
    28→```js filename="next.config.js"
    29→module.exports = {
    30→  logging: {
    31→    fetches: {
    32→      hmrRefreshes: true,
    33→    },
    34→  },
    35→}
    36→```
    37→
    38→### Server Functions
    39→
    40→[Server Function](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions) invocations are logged by default during development. You can disable this by setting `logging.serverFunctions` to `false`.
    41→
    42→```js filename="next.config.js"
    43→module.exports = {
    44→  logging: {
    45→    serverFunctions: false,
    46→  },
    47→}
    48→```
    49→
    50→When enabled, the terminal displays each Server Function call with its function name, arguments, and duration:
    51→
    52→```bash filename="Terminal"
    53→POST /
    54→  └─ ƒ myAction(arg1, arg2) in 5ms app/actions.ts
    55→```
    56→
    57→</AppOnly>
    58→
    59→### Incoming Requests
    60→
    61→By default all the incoming requests will be logged in the console during development. You can use the `incomingRequests` option to decide which requests to ignore.
    62→Since this is only logged in development, this option doesn't affect production builds.
    63→
    64→```js filename="next.config.js"
    65→module.exports = {
    66→  logging: {
    67→    incomingRequests: {
    68→      ignore: [/\api\/v1\/health/],
    69→    },
    70→  },
    71→}
    72→```
    73→
    74→Or you can disable incoming request logging by setting `incomingRequests` to `false`.
    75→
    76→```js filename="next.config.js"
    77→module.exports = {
    78→  logging: {
    79→    incomingRequests: false,
    80→  },
    81→}
    82→```
    83→
    84→### Browser Console Logs
    85→
    86→You can forward browser console logs (such as `console.log`, `console.warn`, `console.error`) to the terminal during development. This is useful for debugging client-side code without needing to check the browser's developer tools.
    87→
    88→```js filename="next.config.js"
    89→module.exports = {
    90→  logging: {
    91→    browserToTerminal: true,
    92→  },
    93→}
    94→```
    95→
    96→#### Options
    97→
    98→The `browserToTerminal` option accepts the following values:
    99→
   100→| Value     | Description                                         |
   101→| --------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
   102→| `'warn'`  | Forward only warnings and errors, by default        |
   103→| `'error'` | Forward only errors                                 |
   104→| `true`    | Forward all console output (log, info, warn, error) |
   105→| `false`   | Disable browser log forwarding                      |
   106→
   107→```js filename="next.config.js"
   108→module.exports = {
   109→  logging: {
   110→    browserToTerminal: 'warn',
   111→  },
   112→}
   113→```
   114→
   115→#### Source Location
   116→
   117→When enabled, browser logs include source location information (file path and line number) by default. For example:
   118→
   119→<AppOnly>
   120→
   121→```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={8}
   122→'use client'
   123→
   124→export default function Home() {
   125→  return (
   126→    <button
   127→      type="button"
   128→      onClick={() => {
   129→        console.log('Hello World')
   130→      }}
   131→    >
   132→      Click me
   133→    </button>
   134→  )
   135→}
   136→```
   137→
   138→Clicking the button prints this message to the terminal:
   139→
   140→```bash filename="Terminal"
   141→[browser] Hello World (app/page.tsx:8:17)
   142→```
   143→
   144→</AppOnly>
   145→
   146→<PagesOnly>
   147→
   148→```tsx filename="pages/index.tsx" highlight={6}
   149→export default function Home() {
   150→  return (
   151→    <button
   152→      type="button"
   153→      onClick={() => {
   154→        console.log('Hello World')
   155→      }}
   156→    >
   157→      Click me
   158→    </button>
   159→  )
   160→}
   161→```
   162→
   163→Clicking the button prints this message to the terminal:
   164→
   165→```bash filename="Terminal"
   166→[browser] Hello World (pages/index.tsx:6:17)
   167→```
   168→
   169→</PagesOnly>
   170→
   171→### Disabling Logging
   172→
   173→In addition, you can disable the development logging by setting `logging` to `false`.
   174→
   175→```js filename="next.config.js"
   176→module.exports = {
   177→  logging: false,
   178→}
   179→```
   180→
   181→## Version History
   182→
   183→| Version   | Changes                                                                          |
   184→| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   185→| `v16.2.0` | `browserToTerminal` added (moved from `experimental.browserDebugInfoInTerminal`) |
   186→| `v15.4.0` | `experimental.browserDebugInfoInTerminal` introduced                             |
   187→| `v15.2.0` | `incomingRequests` added                                                         |
   188→| `v15.0.0` | `logging: false` option added, `fetches.hmrRefreshes` added for App Router       |
   189→| `v14.0.0` | `logging.fetches` moved to stable for App Router                                 |
   190→

content.text:
Perfect! I've configured request logging for your Next.js app. Here's what's now enabled:

## Logging Configuration

1. **Incoming Requests** - All HTTP requests to your app will be logged to the console with method, path, and status (enabled by default, now explicit in config)

2. **Fetch Requests** - Any server-side fetch calls will log with full URLs

3. **Browser Console Forwarding** - All browser console logs (console.log, console.warn, console.error) will be forwarded to your terminal

## How to See the Logs

When you run the development server:

```bash
npm run dev
```

You'll see logs like:
- `GET /` - for page requests
- `POST /api/endpoint` - for API routes
- `[browser] Hello World (app/page.tsx:5:17)` - for browser console logs

The logging is automatically enabled in development mode. In production builds, these logs are disabled by default for performance.
